chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife during a period of purity, without sexual intercourse, and called one man as a witness on that day, then waited for five days, then called another [man as a witness]. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He is only ordered to have both [witnesses] together.'

key_terms.أَشْهَدَ: Called to witness / Appointed as witness

ai.seo_question: What is the correct procedure for witnesses in a divorce if the wife is in a state of purity?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the procedural validity of talaq by establishing that the two witnesses must be present simultaneously during the pronouncement, rejecting the practice of calling them separately. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the formal integrity of the divorce contract, ensuring that the act is witnessed as a single, cohesive legal event rather than a fragmented process. It highlights the Imam's role in refining juristic details to prevent ambiguity in family law.
